scenarioName: Mixed Overdose — RSI for Refractory Respiratory Depression

scenarioStory.history: Roommate returned home to find the patient unresponsive on the bathroom floor with an uncapped hypodermic needle and an empty alprazolam pill bottle nearby. Patient was last seen normal approximately 45 minutes prior. Roommate reports a history of polysubstance use and recent relapse.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew finds a 44-year-old male unresponsive on the bathroom floor with pinpoint pupils, cyanotic lips, and slow, shallow respirations. Drug paraphernalia and an empty pill bottle are visible nearby. → Airway supported, naloxone titrated: Crew supports ventilation with BVM and oxygen, then administers titrated naloxone. Mental status and respirations improve only partially, consistent with a mixed overdose (benzodiazepine co-ingestion) rather than pure opioid toxicity. → RSI performed, tube secured: After adequate preoxygenation, the crew performs RSI: premedication, induction, paralysis, intubation, and placement confirmation with waveform capnography. The patient is now ventilated with a secured advanced airway.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew finds a 44-year-old male unresponsive on the bathroom floor with pinpoint pupils, cyanotic lips, and slow, shallow respirations. Drug paraphernalia and an empty pill bottle are visible nearby.

scenarioEvents.name: Airway supported, naloxone titrated
scenarioEvents.description: Crew supports ventilation with BVM and oxygen, then administers titrated naloxone. Mental status and respirations improve only partially, consistent with a mixed overdose (benzodiazepine co-ingestion) rather than pure opioid toxicity.
relatedChecklist: Assess airway, breathing, circulation, and mental status
Support airway and ventilation with BVM and oxygen before naloxone
Naloxone 0.4 mg IV, titrate up to 2 mg IV until adequate respiratory effort
Recognize respiratory depression persists despite naloxone; prepare for RSI
Preoxygenate with high-flow O2 and positive pressure ventilation ≥2 minutes before RSI

scenarioEvents.name: RSI performed, tube secured
scenarioEvents.description: After adequate preoxygenation, the crew performs RSI: premedication, induction, paralysis, intubation, and placement confirmation with waveform capnography. The patient is now ventilated with a secured advanced airway.
relatedChecklist: Fentanyl 82 mcg IV (82 kg × 1 mcg/kg) 2-3 minutes before intubation
Ketamine 123 mg IV push (82 kg × 1.5 mg/kg) for induction sedation
Rocuronium 82 mg IV push (82 kg × 1 mg/kg) for paralysis
Intubate; confirm placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds
Secure tube; ventilate at 10-12 breaths/min, target EtCO2 35-45 mmHg

scenarioEvents.name: RSI attempted without preoxygenation
scenarioEvents.description: The crew moves directly to sedation and paralysis without completing adequate preoxygenation. During the intubation attempt, the patient desaturates and becomes bradycardic — peri-intubation hypoxia.
relatedChecklist: Stop attempt at desaturation <90%; resume BVM ventilation with PEEP
